name: Dual Volume Rendering
definition: A visualization method where one quantity is color-mapped onto the isocontours (isobars) of another quantity, allowing the investigation of correlations between plasma properties (e.g., magnetic pressure and density) while preserving visibility of steep gradients.
summary: Dual Volume Rendering visualizes two scalar fields by using one field's opacity to define structure and the other's color for content, revealing correlations that overlaid rendering conceals.
